author: sonnet
label: climb-04-01
changes: Added a short Terms section (version, flags, orchestrator, outbox, drainer, fence) so newcomers have the vocabulary before the design decisions.
Step 3: added the numbered order of one write (fence, write, snapshot, outbox row, commit, Postgres apply, outbox delete) and how the drainer relates to it.
Step 3: stated what happens to users outside the dual-write bucket (no outbox, backfill covers them later).
Step 2: explained the email unique conflict with a concrete example and what resolves it.
Step 5: stated that backfill continues past a skipped row and what happens if the drainer hits the same conflict.
Step 6: spelled out the chunk-mismatch procedure as four numbered steps.
Step 9: clarified what each instance does during the 30 s flag window and why Postgres cannot be written before the fence opens.
Added an Open questions section noting the unspecified source of the orchestrator instance count.
Removed the unused epoch from both fences (steps 1, 9, Terms), because nothing read it.
Terms: defined the fence as one switch per database, with the Postgres fence being the migration_state.pg_write_open column.
Design decisions: stated that only user writes are fenced, and that sync copies skip the fence (fixes the contradiction in step 9 item 6).
Step 3: added a short note that the inline apply and the drainer running together is harmless, because of the advisory lock and the version rule.
Step 9: the script now pauses the compare worker at t0 and resumes it at the end, so the outbox drain can reach zero. The drain is polled by the script.
Step 9 item 6: spelled out the Postgres optimistic-lock update, the mirror outbox row, and the explicit-id create mirrored into MySQL.
Step 9: added what clients and reads see during the pause.
Step 10: the rollback also pauses the compare worker, and step 6 notes the pauses.
Reordered into the newcomer layout: summary (with how the system works today), terms, shared rules, rollout steps, open questions.
Merged the 'Design decisions' section and scattered rules into one 'Rules that hold throughout' section, defined once and no longer repeated inside steps.
Merged the repeated persistent-drain-failure and email-conflict explanations (step 2, step 5) into one rule that steps 5 and 6 refer to.
Dropped the separate Flags/outbox/fence design bullets that duplicated Terms; shortened Terms to one-line definitions.
Cut the repeated explanations in step 9 of why the fence protects the Postgres side, and the duplicate 'before step 5' fence note.
Trimmed the step 3 failure bullets and step 11 detail; removed the 'compare worker keeps running' duplication in steps 6 and 8.
Removed internal cross-reference codes in prose where possible and numbered the sub-steps so each step stands alone.
Kept all checklist steps, the 90 s pause limit, 14-day window, 3-day soak and rollback behaviour unchanged.
